messages:
alex.w: Heads up — we started seeing a regression on multi-GPU runs after the CUDA-graph change earlier today. pstep latency went from ~3.2ms to ~5.8ms on a 8xA100 tensor+pipeline config. nvprof timeline shows compute waiting on comms.

maria: Which commit/PR? can you repro on a small model?

alex.w: PR is 4f2d9b8 (cuda-graph: capture stream switch). Repro on smaller gpt-2-ish model with --tp=2 --pp=2. Quick repro command: `./run_inference --model small --tp 2 --pp 2 --batch 4 --seq 512`

jordan: I think I've seen this with graph capture + NCCL before — graph capture can change stream/event visibility and break comm/compute overlap. Did you check whether NCCL ops are captured to the same stream?

alex.w: Good call. nvprof snippet:
```
[Timeline]
compute kernel A: 0ms - 2.8ms
all-reduce start: 2.9ms
cudaStreamWaitEvent: 2.9ms - 5.7ms (blocking compute)
all-reduce end: 5.7ms
```
Looks like compute is blocked by `cudaStreamWaitEvent` until all-reduce finishes. When I disable graph capture the overlap is restored.

kevin: Did you try forcing NCCL onto the capture stream explicitly? Events recorded outside a captured graph are not guaranteed to be visible inside it. NVidia doc warns about event semantics with capture.

alex.w: I tried two things: 1) remove `cudaGraphCreate`/instantiate around the step -> good perf. 2) move NCCL calls to the default stream -> still bad.

maria: Hmm. maybe the graph capture is wrapping the compute stream so events used to synchronize comms are now graph-local and waiting behaves differently. Any CUDA errors/logs?

alex.w: No CUDA error codes, just stalls. Cuprof shows `cudaGraphInstantiate` quickly, but once instantiated the per-iteration kernels are enqueued into the captured graph and the runtime uses `cudaGraphLaunch`. The runtime's `cudaEventRecord` + `cudaStreamWaitEvent` we use for comm/compute handshake seem ineffective under capture.

jordan: There's a known caveat: `cudaEventRecord` inside a graph is not the same as host-recorded events. If the event is recorded while the graph is captured, its scope is the graph node. That can prevent cross-stream sync that previously allowed overlap.

alex.w: Exactly. So behaviour matrix:
- no-graph: overlap (good)
- graph capture global: overlap lost (bad)
- graph capture but disable NCCL capture (tried env var) -> overlap restored (good)

kevin: Can we set a short-term env toggle to disable graph capture for collective ops? Might be the fastest rollback. Also add a perf test to CI to catch this.

alex.w: Added a quick local env var: `REDWOOD_DISABLE_CUDAGRAPH_FOR_NCCL=1` — toggling that flips perf back to baseline in my tests. I'll open a PR to add that switch and a canary rollout.

maria: Please include a minimal reproducer and timeline screenshots in the PR. Also add unit/perf test that runs small multi-gpu scenario and asserts pstep < 4ms.

jordan: For a medium-term fix we should change runtime to: explicitly place NCCL work into a non-captured stream that is promoted to host-sync semantics or use `cudaGraphAddMemcpyNode`/child-graphs for comm nodes. But need to be careful — child graphs and NCCL interactions are subtle.

alex.w: Agreed. I'll prototype two approaches: 1) runtime-level NCCL-on-host-stream that we don't capture, and 2) capture everything but use host-side synchronization for NCCL (extra latency risk). I'll post perf comparisons.

kevin: Also file an issue to upstream perf regression dashboard so we know when this regresses in future. Tag it `regression:cuda-graph-nccl`.

alex.w: Filed: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RINF-1229 (includes logs + repro).

maria: Can infra schedule a canary tomorrow with `REDWOOD_DISABLE_CUDAGRAPH_FOR_NCCL=1` on dedicated pool? @infra-bot

infra-bot: Canary scheduled on redwood-dedicated-us-west for 2026-03-19T02:00Z. Notifying on-call.

jordan: Quick note: if you add a regression test, make it toggle in CI (both with and without graph capture) so we won't miss this class of bug.

alex.w: Will do. Plan: PR for env toggle + tests today, canary tomorrow, longer-term design doc for child-graph/stream changes.

maria: :thumbsup: keep this thread updated with perf numbers.

kevin: :eyes:
